title: Private upgrades: add upgrade plan generator (staged plan + artifact validation + auditable summary)
author: Devon Price
release_notes:
- Adds `redwood-private upgrade plan` to generate a staged, versioned upgrade plan artifact and summary.
- Validates required artifacts (charts/images/bundle manifest) before executing upgrades.
- Persists plan + inputs digest for auditability and support bundles (follow-up PR will wire support bundle ingestion).
commits: planner: introduce stage/step model with stable IDs + schema version
artifacts: resolve sources (online registry vs local bundle) and validate availability
io: persist plan artifact + plan summary + input digests
tests: golden tests for plan generation + artifact validation unit tests
body: Summary This PR introduces an upgrade plan generator to `redwood-private-installer` as the first building block for the Private upgrade + rollback mechanism. The generator produces a staged plan (control-plane first, then data-plane), validates required artifacts before any changes are made, and writes an auditable plan artifact + human-readable summary to disk. Motivation/Context We need a safe-by-default workflow for Redwood Private upgrades (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) with deterministic execution, clear failure modes, and artifacts that can be attached to support bundles and audit logs. The plan generator is intentionally separated from execution so operators (and Release Eng/SRE) can review what will happen before they run it. This aligns with ENG-4821 and the rollout UX direction in DES-311. What’s included - New CLI: `redwood-private upgrade plan` - Produces a versioned plan artifact (schema v1) with stable stage/step IDs. - Stages are ordered and explicit (preflight placeholder, artifact validation, backup placeholder, control-plane rollout placeholder, data-plane rollout placeholder, post-verify placeholder). Execution wiring will come in follow-up PRs; this PR focuses on plan generation and validation. - Artifact validation (fail-fast) - Validates the presence and resolvability of required artifacts for the target version: Helm chart references, required container images (by digest when available), and (when `--airgapped-bundle` is provided) bundle manifest presence and checksum file presence. Signature verification is intentionally out of scope here and will follow in PR-4871. - Produces actionable error messages including the specific missing artifact and the remediation hint (e.g., “configure --artifact-mirror” / “rebuild bundle” / “check registry connectivity”). - Auditable outputs - Writes the plan JSON and a summary text file under `${STATE_DIR}/upgrade-plans/<timestamp>-<from>-to-<to>/`. - Captures: planner version, schema version, CLI args (redacted), input digests (cluster ID, target version, artifact source), and a deterministic plan hash. - Summary includes a step table with stage IDs, blocking validations, and estimated operator prompts. Operator UX Example `redwood-private upgrade plan --from 1.18.2 --to 1.19.0 --artifact-source registry --state-dir /var/lib/redwood-private` Output (abridged): - Plan written: /var/lib/redwood-private/upgrade-plans/2025-04-24T18-22-10Z-1.18.2-to-1.19.0/plan.json - Summary written: /var/lib/redwood-private/upgrade-plans/2025-04-24T18-22-10Z-1.18.2-to-1.19.0/summary.txt - Plan hash: sha256:7b1c… Stages: - validate.artifacts (blocking) - backup.capture (blocking; placeholder until ENG-4838) - rollout.control_plane (blocking; placeholder until chart phase split lands) - rollout.data_plane (blocking; placeholder) - verify.post_upgrade (blocking; placeholder) Notes on determinism and safety - Stage and step IDs are stable across repeated runs for the same inputs; the only non-deterministic value is the output directory timestamp. The plan hash is computed over a canonical JSON form that excludes the timestamped path. - The plan generator does not attempt cluster mutations. It only reads config and validates artifact accessibility (network reachability checks are not included here; those will be part of preflight checks in PR-4834). Tests - Added unit tests for: - schema serialization and canonicalization - stable plan IDs across runs - artifact validation error surfaces - Golden plan fixtures for a handful of common configs (online registry, mirror, air-gapped bundle). Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Preflight check framework + checks (ENG-4829 / PR-4834) - Backup orchestration + snapshot hooks (ENG-4838 / PR-4850) - Rollback command and state machine (ENG-4844 / PR-4862) - Bundle signature verification + stricter offline validation (PR-4871) - Version compatibility gating integration (redwood PR-29104) Review notes - Please focus review on: plan schema shape, determinism, error messages/remediation hints, and state-dir file layout. - The plan schema is intentionally minimal and forward-compatible; we can extend with rollback hooks and migration markers once execution exists. Reviewer discussion highlights - Connor O’Brien: Requested schema version field and explicit “blocking” attribute per stage for change-management gating; addressed in commit “planner: schema_v1”. - Sean Gallagher: Asked for plan artifact redaction to avoid leaking registry creds/headers; CLI arg capture now redacts values for `--registry-password`, `--token`, and any env var expansion with `*_TOKEN`. - Kenji Nakamura: Requested summary output to be operator-first (step table + next actions) rather than raw JSON dump; summary formatter added and default output now includes a short table. - Sahana Iyer: Flagged a flaky golden test on Windows path separators in CI; normalized path rendering in tests and re-ran CI successfully. Merge outcome Squash-merged to main after approvals (Connor O’Brien, Sean Gallagher) and CI green. No runtime behavior changes until the execution path is wired; this is a new command and new internal planner package.
